summary: @onereach/authorizer-helper ships preinstall Bun-runtime dropper that executes obfuscated sibling bundle
details: package.json declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs is itself obfuscated (hex-mangled identifiers, string-map jump tables) and, when the `bun` binary is not on PATH, downloads a platform-specific Bun release from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/, extracts it to a temp directory, marks it executable, and invokes it against the sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 727KB Bun-CJS bundle heavily protected with an obfuscator.io-style shuffled string/number array, a rotator function, and a custom Base85-style decoder — its contents cannot be reasoned about from the surface. The package advertises itself as a small Authorizer 2 helper and index.js only references moment and `loadsh`; nothing in the declared purpose requires the Bun runtime or a 727KB obfuscated payload. Metadata further mismatches the shipped code: the `dependencies` list includes `loadsh@^0.0.4`, a known typosquat of `lodash`, pulled in transitively on install. The alternate-runtime dropper pattern — a Node-declared package fetching a non-Node runtime specifically to execute an obfuscated bundled payload at install time — hides the payload from Node-focused inspection and executes arbitrary attacker-controlled code on the installer's machine on `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
